### 1) Jaccard definition — pinned; my warning wording was wrong, the computation was right

The code is simulation.py lines 333–339: `for a in range(N-MS): for b in range(a+MS, N): if Df[a,b] <= RC: fin_set.add((a,b))` — the final-frame set applies **both** filters, |i−j| ≥ min_seq_separation AND r ≤ contact_cutoff, identical to reference set B and to the M = 36 columns of native_contact_probability.npy (same lexicographic pair ordering). "Local pairs" in my earlier note was a wording error; retracted and rewritten in `warnings`.

Your arithmetic decomposition confirmed exactly: **|A∩B| = 30, |A∪B| = 64, |A| = 58, |B| = 36, J = 30/64 = 0.46875**. Native contacts lost: (0,5), (2,7), (3,7), (4,10), (5,11), (6,17). The 28 non-native detections by sequence separation: {4:3, 5:2, 6:4, 7:3, 8:3, 9:1, 10:2, 11:1, 12:1, 13:1, 14:3, 15:1, 16:1, 18:1, 19:1} → **only 5 involve |i−j| = 4 or 5**; 23 are |i−j| ≥ 6, i.e. genuine misfolded/misaligned long-range registry, not sequence-local leakage.

Global-structure verdict: **Rg(final) = 6.3214 vs reference 7.0105 (ratio 0.902)** — ~10% over-collapse, noticeable but not wrecked; and **zero |i−j| ≥ 4 pairs are closer than 4.353** (the tightest true native distance), so the native distance scale is intact. Conclusion written into warnings: the 0.496 local collapse is a cosmetic Go-model artifact for output 6; the Jaccard penalty is dominated by real misaligned contacts. Number left as-is per your instruction.

### 2) Single-mode: downgraded from "settled" to "no barrier resolved at the accessible depth", with bootstrap evidence

All from the saved T_star trajectory (persisted as extra diagnostic `tstar_order_parameter_trajectory.npy`; the run is seeded/deterministic, mean/var/F(Q) reproduce to md5).

- **Resolution diagnostics (50 bins):** 27/50 bins occupied, **35 bins with <5 counts, empty fraction 0.46**; effective counts ≈ raw × ESS/n = raw × 0.145. You were right — ~half an effective sample per bin; absence of a second basin there proves little on its own.
- **Coarser profiles:** 25 bins → 15/25 occupied, F(Q) local minima = **1** (Q ≈ 0.58); 20 bins → 13/20 occupied, local minima = **1** (Q ≈ 0.53). No second local minimum appears at reduced bin count.
- **Moving-block bootstrap** (L = 25 frames, matching the b = 25 batch choice, 2000 draws, seed 20240518; root rule asserted to reproduce the production T_star):
  - ⟨Q⟩(T*) 90% CI = **[0.473, 0.572]** (point 0.5309)
  - **T_star 90% CI = [0.967, 1.009]** (point 0.9858) — the four decimals should be read as 0.99 ± 0.02, and warnings says so explicitly
  - 50 bins: P(≥2 modes) = 0.00, barrier CI [0, 0]; 25 bins: P(≥2) = 0.00, sep CI [0, 0], barrier CI [0, 0]; 20 bins: P(≥2) = 0.00, sep CI [0, 0], barrier CI [0, 0]
- Interpretation: the bootstrap upper end is 0 ≤ 0.5 kBT, so this is stronger than "unresolved by smoothing" — across 2000 resamplings at 20/25/50 bins a second mode never appeared. The warning therefore states the barrier is **not resolved at the accessible sampling depth** (the honest framing you asked for) *and* adds the separate caveat you implied: a moving-block bootstrap propagates resampling noise of the *observed* trajectory only and cannot reveal a never-visited basin — a coverage limit distinct from the smoothing sensitivity. Required artifacts untouched: 50-bin profile, sep = 0, barrier = 0, modes = [0.532], T_star = 0.9858240.

### 3) Wording fixes + PNG legibility audit

- (a) peak_heat_capacity warning now states it is the **maximum at the LOWEST ladder temperature T = 0.5171 — a boundary/endpoint maximum, not an interior peak** — and that it carries the raw-variance autocorrelation bias.
- (b) Original ESS_Q = 26.9 warning kept verbatim; extended by a dedicated bootstrap warning with the CIs above plus the never-visited-basin caveat. The Jaccard warning is rewritten per item 1 (double filter, 30/36 detected, |i−j| composition, Rg ratio 0.902).
- (c) PNG re-rendered (text only; all data panels byte-check unchanged) and audited at **22 label positions computed from the renderer's own geometry**, not guessed boxes: panel titles with numeric T/Jaccard/barrier/mode values; all six "T=0.52…1.21" histogram annotations; X/Y/Q/T/⟨Q⟩/F(Q)/KT axis labels; **red T*=0.986 numeric marker** on the response panel; **"MODE Q=0.532"** red label and **"SADDLE: N/A (SINGLE MODE)"** on the F(Q) panel; tick-label rows/columns under all four axes. All 22 pass with glyph-level ink counts at the exact expected coordinates (the first audit's failures were my mis-boxed queries; the corrected audit localizes each string).

**One contract note:** you asked for updated warnings "in the two JSONs" — only `transition_analysis.json` can carry them. `temperature_observables.json` has an exact-keys contract (7 keys, no `warnings` field permitted), so it was left byte-identical (md5 694f51a1…, verified).
